key_insight: VISOR reduces LVLM inference cost by keeping full visual representations but making vision-language interactions sparse and dynamically requested — preserving fine-grained performance without compressing or discarding visual tokens.
problem_solved: Existing efficiency methods compress visual tokens into a bottleneck that hurts performance on detailed reasoning and fine-grained tasks; VISOR targets compute reduction without sacrificing visual information or task accuracy.
method: Keep full visual feature maps available and avoid aggressive token reduction; do not throw away visual information.
Use a lightweight, learned request/gating mechanism that decides at runtime which queries or prompts require visual context, triggering cross-modal interactions only when needed.
Implement sparse, dynamic cross-attention paths so only a subset of tokens or layers access vision features, cutting compute and latency while retaining accuracy on hard visual-language reasoning.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy LVLMs that are both efficient and accurate on challenging multimodal tasks — reducing inference cost and latency without the accuracy trade-offs of token-compression approaches, making scalable multimodal systems more practical.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM + vision encoder with an on-request/gating module that selectively opens cross-modal paths.
Cost vs. accuracy bar/line chart comparing baseline visual-token-reduction methods to VISOR (lower compute, equal/higher accuracy).
Sequence illustration: examples showing when the model skips vision vs when it requests visual context for a fine-grained question.
Sparse attention heatmap: visualizing which tokens/layers access vision features over time to convey dynamic sparsity.
paper_title: VISion On Request: Enhanced VLLM efficiency with sparse, dynamically selected, vision-language interactions
paper_authors: Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Yassine Ouali, Georgios Tzimiropoulos
